claims.text: The local source slice models two Hyper CoroCoro Spring 1999 issue insert rows: Pikachu row 086 and Jigglypuff row 087.
The local source rows derive from Bulbapedia raw wikitext rows 086-087, both carrying the promotion note Hyper CoroCoro Spring 1999 issue insert (March 1, 1999).
The local source rows mark both cards as English w/Gray Star and point to Wizards Promo identities: Pikachu Wizards Promo 1 and Jigglypuff Wizards Promo 7.

This source slice matters because the cards are English-language Wizards Promo designs moving through a Japanese Hyper CoroCoro magazine route, so language, symbol, and distribution route must all survive matching.

Agents should preserve Hyper CoroCoro Spring 1999 route, March 1 1999 date, row 086-087 pair identity, English w/Gray Star variant note, gray-star/yellow-PROMO symbol context, and non-equivalence with ordinary English Wizards Black Star, October 1996 glossy CoroCoro, Base, Jungle, Song Best, and later mascot memories before accepting a match.

narrative.human_title: Hyper CoroCoro Spring 1999 — English promos inside a Japanese magazine
narrative.why_it_matters: This little two-card insert is a perfect protocol problem. Pikachu and Jigglypuff look like familiar English Wizards promos, but the route is not simply English retail memory; the source slice says Hyper CoroCoro Spring 1999, March 1, 1999. That means the agent cannot stop at name, language, or gray star. It has to keep the magazine route alive. The romance is small and very CoroCoro: two mascot-weight cards crossing language and market boundaries through a kid's magazine object, making the franchise feel wider than one country's checklist.

narrative.human_title: Pikachu — the English promo that still needs a Japanese magazine route
narrative.why_it_matters: Pikachu is the dangerous one because every collector already thinks they know it. Here, that confidence is the trap. The card is an English Wizards Promo identity, yes, but the source slice cares about a Japanese magazine route: Hyper CoroCoro Spring 1999. The gray star, yellow PROMO, and Keiji Kinebuchi correction context help orient the card, but they do not replace the route. A good agent should feel the mascot gravity and still slow down.

narrative.human_title: Jigglypuff — the quiet proof that this was a pair
narrative.why_it_matters: Jigglypuff is not the loud card in this insert, and that is why it earns its keep. Pikachu gets the spotlight; Jigglypuff proves the route. It ties the Hyper CoroCoro Spring 1999 source note to a two-card magazine object and asks the agent to respect the pair rather than chase mascot gravity. Kagemaru Himeno's soft character language fits the card beautifully, but the collector work is still route work: English w/Gray Star, gray PROMO symbol, Japanese magazine insert, row 087.
